simple: This page walks you through making your own move for the Character Controller Library (CCL): a dash that shoots the character forward, then makes them wait 1 second before dashing again. You write the ability in a ModuleScript, then register it for every character from a server Script. Once you understand this one, you can build wall jumps, aiming, and other special moves the same way.
analogy: Making an ability is like writing a recipe card (the ModuleScript) and then handing a copy to every cook in the kitchen (registering it on each character). The card says when to start, how long to cook, and how long to let the pan cool.
keyPoints: Turn on CCL first in Beta Features and Avatar Settings.
Put a ModuleScript named `Dash` in a `CustomAbilities` folder in `ReplicatedStorage`, so the server and players can both use it.
The dash loop: start on the ground when not cooling down, run while the 0.2-second `DashWindow` label lasts, then add a 1-second `DashCooldown` label.
`Input = { InputName = "Dash", Mode = "Press", ActionSlot = 5 }` starts the dash on a press of slot 5, which is the left mouse button or gamepad R2.
The `OnStart` callback does the actual push with `rootPart:ApplyImpulse()`, in the direction the character faces.
Register abilities on the server with `AvatarAbilities.addAbilityForCharacter(character, abilityModule)`. Pass the module itself, do not `require` it.
Callbacks run on both the player's device and the server, so keep them deterministic.

terms.AbilityDefinition: The table that describes one ability: its name, when it starts, what stops it, and its code.
terms.ModuleScript: A script that returns a value, like a table, so other scripts can use it.
terms.register: Add an ability to a character so the CCL starts checking and running it.
terms.TimedLabels: Labels that turn on for a set number of seconds and then turn off by themselves, like `DashWindow = 0.2`.
terms.cooldown: A waiting time before you can use the ability again, here 1 second.
terms.impulse: An instant shove. `ApplyImpulse` pushes a part once, like kicking a ball.
terms.RootLookVector: The direction the character is facing, as a `Vector3` of length 1.
terms.AssemblyMass: The total mass of all parts stuck together with the root part. Multiplying by it makes the push feel the same for heavy and light characters.
terms.AbilityManagerActor: An object inside the character that runs the ability system. The register script waits for it before adding abilities.
terms.predicted client simulation: The player's device guesses the result right away so movement feels instant, while the server does the official version.
terms.deterministic: Gives the same result every time from the same starting point, so the client's guess and the server agree.

example.title: Register custom abilities on every character
example.place: Script named RegisterCustomAbilities in ServerScriptService (with the Dash ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage > CustomAbilities)
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local AvatarAbilities = require("@rbx/AvatarAbilities")

-- List every custom ability module here
local CUSTOM_ABILITIES = {
	ReplicatedStorage.CustomAbilities.Dash,
}

local function onCharacterAdded(character)
	-- Wait for the ability system inside the character
	local actor = character:WaitForChild("AbilityManagerActor", 10)
	if not actor then
		return
	end
	while not actor:IsDescendantOf(game) do
		actor.AncestryChanged:Wait()
	end

	-- Add each ability (pass the module, do not require it)
	for _, abilityModule in CUSTOM_ABILITIES do
		AvatarAbilities.addAbilityForCharacter(character, abilityModule)
	end
end

local function onPlayerAdded(player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded)
	if player.Character then
		task.spawn(onCharacterAdded, player.Character)
	end
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	onPlayerAdded(player)
end
explain: `CUSTOM_ABILITIES` lists the ModuleScripts to add. You can add more abilities to this list later.
When a character spawns, we wait up to 10 seconds for its `AbilityManagerActor`, then make sure it is really in the game.
`addAbilityForCharacter` gives that character the Dash ability.
Now pressing the left mouse button (slot 5) on the ground makes the character dash forward, then wait 1 second before dashing again.

watchOut: Calling `require()` on the ability module in the register script. Pass the module object itself to `addAbilityForCharacter`.
Registering abilities from a LocalScript. Registration must happen on the server.
Adding `task.wait()` inside `OnStart` to time the dash. Callbacks must not yield, so use `TimedLabels` for timing.
Naming two ModuleScripts or abilities the same. Each needs a unique name.
